key_insight: A large-scale, temporally coherent dataset captured from AAA games using a novel dual-screen stitched technique provides synchronized RGB and multi-channel G-buffers at scale, bridging the realism and temporal-coherence gap that limits generative inverse and forward rendering.
problem_solved: Existing synthetic datasets lack realism and temporal coherence, limiting the scalability and real-world transfer of generative inverse/forward rendering models.
method: Dual-screen stitched capture to extract synchronized RGB plus five G-buffer channels at 720p/30FPS, producing 4M continuous frames.
Curation from visually complex AAA game environments to capture diverse scenes, dynamic effects, materials, and consistent temporal sequences.
Package the dataset for training and evaluation of temporally-aware generative rendering tasks (e.g., relighting, material estimation, neural video rendering).
impact: Provides practitioners a high-fidelity, temporally-consistent training and evaluation resource that reduces domain gap and enables more robust, real-world-capable generative rendering and video-consistent neural models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram of the dual-screen stitched capture method (hardware/logic blocks).

Timeline / strip of consecutive frames illustrating temporal continuity (30 FPS) across scenes.
Bar/line chart comparing model performance or domain gap when trained on prior synthetic datasets vs. this AAA-derived dataset.
paper_authors: Zheng-Hui Huang, Zhixiang Wang, Jiaming Tan, Ruihan Yu, Yidan Zhang
